whats_new.title: What's new in 6.0
steps: Backups now contain everything: every record and every detail. A backup that can't read part of the data stops with an error instead of saving an incomplete copy.
Sync between devices now carries edits and deletions, so a correction made on one phone reaches the others and deleted entries stay deleted.
Emergency plan in Settings → Recording: set the alert time and what counts as a cluster to match your care plan. The alert counts seizure time, not the aura or recovery.
If there was no aura, just tap End seizure. The seizure type can be changed from the summary.
After-seizure symptoms are grouped, record where they were felt (numbness, weakness, paralysis…), and how long it took to get back to normal.
Saved symptom sets belong to a seizure type and are offered after you choose it, with your most-used symptoms. Symptoms you type yourself are remembered.
Back always returns to where you were, with History's filters kept. Restoring onto a new phone can copy all its settings too.

recording.title: Recording a Seizure
steps: Tap the large START button when a seizure begins.
In Caretaker mode, tap the phase buttons (End Aura, End Seizure) as each phase transitions. In Self mode the interface is simplified to a single stop button.
Tap + Event Note to stamp a timestamped note mid-recording — use the shortcut buttons for common events like Fell, Rescue Med given, Not Responding, etc.
Tap STOP when the seizure ends. If the timer is still running at 12 minutes, the recording stops automatically and the event is saved.

tagging.title: Tagging Events
steps: After stopping, a tagging wizard opens automatically.
Select the seizure type, affected body regions, and any symptoms observed.
Add free-text notes, then tap SAVE. You can edit any event later from History.

manual.title: Manual Entry
steps: Tap + Log Past Seizure on the home screen to enter a seizure you did not record in real time.
Set the date, time, and duration, then complete the tagging wizard as usual.

medications.title: Medication Tracking
steps: Add your medications in Settings → Medications.
Use OD, BD, TDS, QDS, PRN, scheduled times, and day-of-week settings to match the prescribed plan.
The home screen shows today's scheduled doses — tap each medication button to toggle it, then tap Save to log the doses.
Medication History shows logged, missed, late, extra, and corrected doses. Edited entries keep an audit marker.

Enable dose reminders per medication in Settings → Medications. Rescue medicines can also be highlighted during emergency alerts. Reminders come while AuraTrack is open or was used recently; for a guaranteed alarm also set one in your phone’s clock.

wellbeing.title: Daily Wellbeing
steps: Use the Daily Wellbeing Check-In to record mood, intensity, notes, and context factors for the day.
Configure wellbeing factors in Settings → Wellbeing. Scale, number, and boolean factors can be enabled or hidden without changing old entries.
The Wellbeing history tab helps compare entries with seizure timing. These patterns are for discussion and do not prove a trigger caused a seizure.
Neurologist reports can chart mood and numeric wellbeing factors as separate lines, with seizures kept visually distinct as bars.

eeg.title: EEG Diary
steps: Turn on EEG diary controls in Settings → Recording when long-term EEG monitoring is needed.
Start an EEG session, then log activities, symptoms, medication changes, sleep, meals, and other clinically useful observations during the session.
Link seizure records when a seizure occurs during the EEG period so the report can connect the diary context to the event.
Export the EEG diary from History → Export when you need a printable session summary.

history.title: History Review
steps: Open History to browse seizures, EEG diary entries, medication history, wellbeing entries, and exports.
Use the seizure filters and trend chart to review events by date, type, and detail status.
Tap any event to view full detail, danger flags, timings, notes, triggers, video reference, edit history, or to edit the event.
Use the medication and wellbeing tabs to review corrections and daily context alongside seizure history.

reports.title: Reports & Exports
steps: Use History → Export to create encrypted backups, CSV files, printable event logs, neurologist reports, monthly seizure diaries, and EEG diary PDFs.
The neurologist report includes medications, adherence counts, event tables, clinical flags, data-quality notes, and charted seizure trends.
Report charts use sans-serif text and strict value-label limits so dense reports stay readable. The wellbeing chart uses seizure bars plus separate mood and numeric/context lines.
AuraTrack does not calculate an average mood intensity score; wellbeing summaries focus on entries, days covered, top moods, top context factors, and recent entries.

sync_backup.title: Sync & Backup
steps: Use encrypted backups for recovery or device migration. The passphrase is required to restore and is not stored by AuraTrack.
Use Easy Sync, Private Sync, or manual encrypted transfer when moving data between devices.
Settings → Data & Backup shows storage protection status, backup reminders, import/export tools, and destructive data actions.
CSV, PDF, video, and backup files are sensitive medical files. Store and share them carefully.

settings.title: Settings & Accessibility
steps: Switch between Self and Caretaker mode in Settings to adjust the interface.
Change language, theme, font size, time format, duration format, and accent colour to suit your preferences.
Add patient details, caregiver details, neurologist information, report notes, and emergency contacts.
Customize quick-note labels, wellbeing reminders, medication reminders, backup reminders, and whether date of birth appears in reports.

about.title: About
about.about_text: AuraTrack is a privacy-first seizure tracking app for people with epilepsy and their caregivers. Record seizures in real time, annotate events with clinical detail, track medications, and generate structured reports for your neurologist — all stored locally on your device.
about.privacy_text: AuraTrack is designed to keep seizure and medication records local-first. By default, your data stays in your browser storage on this device and is only shared when you deliberately export, print, or sync it.

local.title: Stored locally
local.body: AuraTrack stores event logs, medications, dose logs, EEG diary entries, and report settings in IndexedDB on your device. The app does not require an account to create or keep these records.

sharing.title: When data is shared
sharing.body: Your health data leaves AuraTrack only when you choose to export a backup or report, print a PDF, save a video recording, or send data to another device during sync.

sync.title: Sync behavior
sync.body: AuraTrack's device-to-device sync uses browser-encrypted transport. Depending on the sync mode, connection or signaling metadata may still pass through the signaling service or your local network.

exports.title: Export security
exports.body: Encrypted backups are protected by the passphrase you choose. Exported CSV, PDF, and video files remain regular files on the destination device.

about.disclaimer_text: AuraTrack is a personal logging tool and is not a medical device. It is not intended to diagnose, treat, or replace professional medical advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider regarding your condition and treatment.
about.opensource_text: AuraTrack is open source. Report bugs or suggest features on GitHub Issues.

data.persistence_detail_flow_prompt: User-initiated request. A browser permission prompt may appear when you tap the button.
data.persistence_detail_flow_auto: Automatic browser decision. The browser may silently grant or deny without showing a permission popup.
data.persistence_detail_browser_webkit: WebKit browsers on iPhone/iPad and Safari-class environments usually decide this silently. Installing the app can help storage quotas, but backups are still essential.
data.persistence_detail_browser_chromium: Chromium browsers such as Chrome and Edge usually decide this from browser heuristics, so tapping again may recheck without showing a prompt.
data.persistence_detail_browser_gecko: Firefox-class browsers may show a permission prompt when requested from this screen.
data.persistence_detail_browser_generic: Browser behavior varies by engine and device.
data.persistence_detail_reason: Exact denial reasons are not exposed by the web API, so AuraTrack can only show the browser result, not why it decided that way.
